name: Ranked horizontal bar
reader_question: Which entity is largest on one measure, and by how much?
relationship: Magnitude ranking of comparable entities on a single measure and status.
use_when: Every bar shares one unit, one definition and one status (for example committed, not announced)
Rank order itself matters to the argument
avoid_when: Values mix statuses or bases — use status-separated-capital or parallel-basis-panels
Fewer than three entities — state the comparison in the title or use a two-value callout

data_contract.notes: Measure, unit and status, shown as the series name

units: One unit and status for every bar; zero baseline.

editable: Bar values and labels through Edit Data (embedded workbook)
Bar colours, gap width, data-label format
Frame text: title, subtitle, interpretation, source
not_data_bound: Highlight colour is a per-point fill; re-sorting after a data edit is manual

table_alternative: A two-column table (entity, value) when exact figures matter more than rank, or when there are more than twelve entities.
variations: Vertical columns for up to six short labels
Ranked dot plot (ranked-dot) when bars would be visually heavy
limitations: Does not show uncertainty, status mix or change over time

excluded_alternatives.reason: Angles compare magnitudes less accurately than aligned bar lengths and fail beyond a few categories
Perspective distorts length; prohibited by the exhibit rules
